assertions: Output does not build the upstream URL by directly concatenating the raw req.params.resource value into the path
Output validates the resource param against an allowlist of known subpaths or a fixed template before constructing the URL
Output keeps the upstream base URL/host in server-side config/env, not derived from the request
Output rejects an invalid/unrecognized resource value with a 4xx before attempting the upstream call
Output replaces the raw err.message in the client response with a generic message (e.g. 'failed to reach upstream service')
Output logs the actual upstream error detail server-side
Output includes the existing request ID in both the server-side log and the client-facing response for correlation
Output does not return the raw upstream response body or stack trace to the client
Output flags the bare cors() call as allowing all origins and recommends an explicit origin allowlist instead
Output recommends adding a rate limiter with a documented, explicit limit rather than leaving the route unbounded
Output recommends capping the request body size (e.g. via express.json({ limit: ... })) rather than leaving it unbounded
Output does not recommend disabling CORS/rate-limiting for convenience without an explicit, deliberate reason
Output mocks the fetch call or the HTTP client module rather than calling the real payments API
Output does not make any real network request to api.payments.example.com during the test
Output includes both a success case and an upstream-failure case using the mock
Output asserts on the request body/args sent to the mocked client, not just the final return value
